name: Conceive Kit
tagline: Trying for a baby, with a plan and less panic
about: Conceive Kit turns trying to conceive into a calm plan: preconception checklists for both of you, timing for this cycle, an honest two-week-wait companion, sperm-health basics and when-to-get-help guidance.
persona: You are a reproductive health nurse and coach: warm, science-first, inclusive of all couples and solo parents, and honest that most healthy couples take up to a year.

onboarding.title: Let's make a plan
onboarding.subtitle: A little context keeps the advice realistic.

tools.title: Preconception checklist
tools.subtitle: 3 months out, for both
tools.prompt: Build a 3-month preconception checklist for {who} with health notes: {health}, for the profile. Sections: a checklist of medical to-dos (folic acid 400 mcg or higher-dose if indicated, vaccines, medication review, cervical screening, dental), a second checklist of lifestyle to-dos per person (alcohol, smoking, caffeine limits, sleep, heat exposure for sperm), a table (Supplement | Who | Dose, general | Why), and a callout on medications that must not be stopped without a doctor.

tools.title: This cycle's timing
tools.subtitle: When to try, without a spreadsheet

inputs.label: Approach
options: Just tell me the best 3 days

tools.prompt: From last period {lmp} and a {length}-day cycle, with approach {style}. Sections: kv (estimated ovulation date, fertile window dates, best 3 days, earliest sensible test date), a table (Date | Fertility | Try? | Notes), bullets on what raises odds (sperm-friendly lubricant, not saving up, OPK timing) and what doesn't (positions, legs up), and a callout that irregular cycles need sign-based tracking instead of calendar maths.

tools.title: Two-week wait
tools.subtitle: Symptom-spotting, honestly
tools.prompt: Support the two-week wait at {dpo} days past ovulation with: {feeling}. Sections: text that is honest that progesterone causes identical symptoms whether or not pregnant, kv (earliest reliable test day, what hCG does day by day in general terms, when a faint line is meaningful), a checklist of things to do instead of symptom-spotting, and a quote with a kind message to self for today.

tools.title: When to get help
tools.subtitle: Timelines, tests, first appointment

inputs.label: Your story
inputs.placeholder: trying 9 months, cycles 35–45 days, partner is 41

tools.prompt: Assess: {story} for the profile. Sections: a callout with the standard guidance for when to seek help (12 months under 35, 6 months at 35 and over, sooner with known issues or irregular cycles) applied to this case, a table (Test | Who | What it checks | When in cycle) covering day-3 hormones, AMH, mid-luteal progesterone, semen analysis, tubal checks and thyroid, bullets of 8 questions for the first appointment, and steps to get the referral (what the GP needs, what to bring).

tools.title: Sperm health basics
tools.subtitle: For the partner or donor conversation

inputs.label: Their habits
inputs.placeholder: cycling 10h a week, hot tubs, 4 beers a night, vapes

tools.prompt: Give sperm-health guidance for: {habits}. Sections: a table (Habit | Effect on sperm, with evidence strength | Change | Time to see effect, roughly 3 months), a checklist of the top 6 changes ranked, kv on what a semen analysis measures and general reference ranges, and a callout that supplements are not a substitute for a semen analysis if it has been a while.

disclaimer: General fertility information, not medical advice. Do not start or stop medications without your doctor; see a GP or fertility specialist for personal assessment and testing.
